content:
Apple has confirmed an issue causing a "small number" of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on the AT&T network to lose cellular service.

Apple has rolled out software and carrier updates to prevent the issue from affecting more users, but the company told 9to5Mac that devices that have already lost service will require hardware replacement.

Apple's statement to 9to5Mac:

The carrier settings update for iPhone 18 Pro Max will be automatically downloaded within the next 14 days. However, users can manually trigger the download by going to "Settings," selecting "General," and then tapping "About."

Apple explained that the software update will help prevent iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T from encountering similar issues in the future. The software update cannot restore connectivity to devices that have already lost service.

Apple says iPhone 18 Pro Max users who have already lost service will need to have their hardware replaced. Those users should contact Apple Support or AT&T, or visit an Apple Store or AT&T retail location in person.

As we reported this morning, iPhone 18 Pro Max users affected by this issue are unable to connect to the AT&T network for calls, texts, and data. The iPhone status bar on affected users will show "SOS." Not all iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T are affected by the connectivity issue.

It is worth noting that the US version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem. As for the iPhone 18 Pro, which uses the Apple C2 modem, it is not affected by this AT&T connectivity issue.
